docs.title: How It's Built
docs.text:
• Static site generator: MkDocs with Material theme
  • Hosting: GitHub Pages — free, public, accessible from any device
  • Editing: Any text editor — VS Code recommended

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text: Feature How Search Press Ctrl+K or click the search bar. Full-text across all pages. Tags Add tags: [tag-name] in a page's frontmatter. See tags for everything. Wiki links Write [[page-name]] and it becomes a clickable link at build time. Code blocks Fenced code with syntax highlighting + copy button on hover. Dark/light mode Click the sun/moon icon in the top bar. File attachments Images, PDFs, code files go in docs/assets/.

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
my-wiki/
├── mkdocs.yml            # Site configuration
├── requirements.txt      # Python dependencies
├── .github/workflows/    # Auto-deploy on push
└── docs/                 # ← All your wiki content lives here
    ├── index.md
    ├── getting-started/
    ├── notes/
    ├── bookmarks/
    ├── code-snippets/
    ├── how-to/
    ├── tags.md
    └── assets/
        ├── images/
        ├── pdfs/
        └── code/

docs.title: Quick Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a new .md file in the right folder under docs/
  2. Add frontmatter with tags at the top of the file
  3. Write your content with [[wiki-links]] to other pages
  4. Preview: mkdocs serve → open http://localhost:8000
  5. Publish: mkdocs gh-deploy (or just push — GitHub Actions auto-deploys)

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
• Filenames: kebab-case → python-tips.md, not Python Tips.md
  • Tags: lowercase, no spaces → tags: [python, beginner, windows]
  • Links: [[file-name]] for wiki pages, [text](https://.../) for external

docs.title: B550 Build (Planned Main Rig Upgrade)
docs.text: Plan: make this the board in the main rig, together with a used Ryzen 5 5600.

docs.title: In Hand
docs.text: • ASUS Prime B550 motherboard, unopened. Bought about six months ago for future builds. The exact model number is on the box and still to confirm.

docs.title: Waiting On
docs.text: • Used Ryzen 5 5600 at a good price

docs.title: Reused From the Main Rig
docs.text: 16GB DDR4, MSI GTX 1060 6GB, EVGA 850W PSU and the NVMe drive.

docs.title: How the Swap Works
docs.text:
B550 boards do not support Ryzen 1000-series CPUs, so the board and the 5600 go in together. Until both are in hand, the X370 stays the daily driver.

  • Back up the NVMe first
  • Debian will boot on the new board, but the network interface name changes (it is enp30s0 now) and the new board has a new MAC address. Update the router's DHCP reservation and the Wake-on-LAN setup afterwards.
  • The Windows 10 drive will want re-activation

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text: The X370 board and the Ryzen 5 1600X become spare parts, and are the candidate for the next home server. See the Homelab Roadmap.

docs.title: X370 Desktop (Main Rig)
docs.text: Daily driver since October 2026. It replaced the X79, which is now the home server.

docs.title: Specs
docs.text: Component Details Motherboard MSI X370 Gaming Pro Carbon (MS-7A32) CPU AMD Ryzen 5 1600X (6C/12T, 3.6 GHz) Cooler Noctua single-tower air cooler GPU MSI GTX 1060 6GB Gaming X RAM 16GB DDR4 Storage ~500GB M.2 NVMe (moved over from the X79), ext4 PSU EVGA SuperNOVA 850 G2 (80+ Gold) Display BenQ XL2411Z 24" 1080p, used while the MSI 165Hz monitor is lent out OS Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12, KDE Plasma 6.3 on Wayland, zsh Network enp30s0, 192.168.50.68

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The board has two M.2 slots. One holds the system NVMe and the other is free. Candidates for the free slot:

  • 256GB M.2 with a working Windows 10 install. Keep it for games that need Windows and pick it from the BIOS boot menu (F11) instead of setting up a GRUB dual boot. Windows 10 is out of support, so use it for games only.
  • 500GB M.2, contents unknown. Mount it read-only first and look at what is on it before wiping anything.

Check whether each drive is NVMe or M.2 SATA before installing it. Which slot supports which, and which SATA ports it disables, is in the board manual.

  • DHCP reservation for 192.168.50.68 on the router
  • Confirm Tailscale is installed and the machine shows up on the tailnet
  • Get the MSI 165Hz monitor back

docs.title: Upgrade Path
docs.text: The plan is a Ryzen 5 5600 on the unopened B550 board. When that happens the X370 board and the 1600X become spare parts and are a candidate for the next home server, see the Homelab Roadmap.

docs.title: X79 Server
docs.text: Former main desktop. Since October 2026 it is the home server, and the X370 rig is the daily driver. It has no monitor of its own: it is used over SSH and the Cockpit web console, and its HDMI output goes to the bedroom TV when it needs a screen.

docs.title: Specs
docs.text: Component Details Case Dutzo, with ARGB fan lighting (see microcontrollers) Motherboard ASUS X79 DELUXE CPU Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 (10C/20T, 2.8 GHz, no AVX2) GPU MSI GTX 1060 6GB Gaming X (secondhand, ~483 kr) RAM 16GB DDR3, mixed Corsair Dominator and Crucial Ballistix, running at 1333MHz (no XMP) Boot drive 128GB SATA SSD (taken from the Acer laptop) Storage 300GB SATA drive OS Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12 Network eth0, 192.168.50.190, Wake-on-LAN set up

docs.title: Running Now
docs.text:
• Jellyfin
  • Cockpit web console on port 9090

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
Docker first, Proxmox later. The machine has a 128GB boot drive and 16GB of RAM, so virtual machines would use up the headroom for no real gain right now. Proxmox is a better fit on the Ryzen box that frees up after the B550 upgrade. A few modern container images assume AVX2, which this CPU lacks, so check an image before pulling it.

  • Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin
  • Move Jellyfin into Compose, with NVENC transcoding on the GTX 1060
  • Bring Pi-hole back as a container
  • Uptime Kuma, and a Samba share for the iPhone Files app
  • Backups to the second drive plus an offsite copy
  • Measure the idle power draw with a wall plug meter

The full order of work is in the Homelab Roadmap. Network layout is on network.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Built from secondhand parts (~1,000–1,500 SEK in total).
  • Ran Windows 10 first, then CachyOS, then Debian 13 with KDE (September 2026).
  • Installed the GTX 1060 and cleared the AMD-to-NVIDIA driver conflicts.
  • Settled on DDR3-1333 (no XMP) after mixing the Corsair and Crucial kits.
  • Fixed an NVIDIA persistence boot error by turning Secure Boot off.
  • Ran Ollama on the 1060.
  • October 2026: the NVMe moved to the X370 rig, the Acer's 128GB SSD became the boot drive, and this machine became the server.

docs.title: Diagnosis / Recovery Ideas
docs.text:
• Check whether the BIOS/UEFI still posts (external monitor over VGA or DP?)
  • The WLAN slot may have shorted power rails, so inspect for burned components near the slot
  • Try a CMOS reset: remove the main battery, disconnect the CMOS battery, hold power for 30s
  • If it is dead, the SSD and RAM can be salvaged

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text:
• Tailscale connects the iPhone and the desktops, so the same SSH commands work at home and away.

  • Wake-on-LAN is set up on the X79.
  • Cockpit (web console) runs on the X79 at port 9090.
  • Claude Code: run it on a desktop and drive the session from the iPhone with Remote Control, so nothing needs to be exposed to the internet.

docs.text:

docs.title: WD Green 1TB (WD10EZRX) — Repair or Replace
docs.text:
• Drive: WD10EZRX, 64MB cache, manufactured March 2013.
  • Problem: bent pins in the SATA power connector. It still shows up in lsblk and works, but it can't be trusted.
  • Next steps:
    1. Read the SMART data (sudo smartctl -a /dev/sdX) and look at reallocated sectors, pending sectors and CRC errors.
    2. Try to straighten the pins under magnification with fine tweezers, or keep the drive as scratch storage only.
    3. For anything that matters, such as the media library or backups, replace it. A 13-year-old drive is a liability.
    4. WD Green drives park their heads after 8 seconds idle. If it goes into a server, disable that with idle3ctl.
  • Status: Needs repair or replacement.

docs.title: Homelab Roadmap
docs.text: Goal: a small, reliable home server setup that I can explain, rebuild from scratch and show to others. One step at a time, and each step is finished and written down before the next one starts.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
• Server now: X79. Debian 13, 16GB RAM, GTX 1060. Cockpit and Jellyfin already run on it.
  • Server later: the X370 board with the Ryzen 5 1600X, once the main rig moves to the B550. It idles lower than the Xeon and has AVX2, which the Xeon lacks.
  • Always-on helpers: the Acer and ASUS laptops, once they have a drive.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Every service lives in its own folder with a Compose file, and the folder is in git. No secrets in git.
  2. If it is not backed up, it does not exist.
  3. Every service gets a wiki page: what it does, how it is set up, how to restore it.

docs.title: Phase 0: Foundations
docs.text:
• DHCP reservations in the router for both desktops
  • Consistent hostnames, SSH key login on every machine, then turn off password login
  • Tailscale on every machine
  • tmux on the servers, and Termius or Blink Shell with Mosh on the iPhone instead of iSH
  • ClientAliveInterval 30 and ClientAliveCountMax 4 in sshd_config
  • Router admin and WiFi passwords changed from the defaults and stored in a password manager

docs.title: Phase 1: Docker on the X79
docs.text:
• Docker Engine and the Compose plugin, installed from Docker's own Debian repository
  • One folder per service under ~/srv/compose/
  • Jellyfin in Compose, with NVIDIA transcoding (nvidia-container-toolkit)
  • Pi-hole in Compose, with the router handing it out as DNS and a fallback DNS server kept
  • Uptime Kuma
  • Samba share for the iPhone Files app
  • Tailscale subnet router and exit node

docs.title: Phase 2: Backups
docs.text:
• restic or borg from the server to a second drive
  • An offsite copy (a cloud bucket, or a USB drive kept somewhere else)
  • Restore test: delete a service folder and bring it back from backup

docs.title: Phase 3: More Services
docs.text:
• Immich for photos
  • Home Assistant
  • Frigate, once there are cameras
  • Ollama on the GTX 1060

docs.title: Phase 4: Proxmox
docs.text: When the Ryzen server is free, install Proxmox on it and run a Debian VM with Docker inside. Practice snapshots, VM backups and moving a service between nodes.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Passwords and API keys go in a password manager. On the servers they are in .env files with chmod 600, listed in .gitignore. If they ever have to be in git, encrypt them first (sops with age).

docs.title: Portfolio Checklist
docs.text:
• A wiki page per service
  • A separate homelab repository with the Compose files and a README
  • A network diagram
  • Screenshots of Cockpit and Uptime Kuma

Planeringsdokument för en eventuell hobbyverksamhet/eget företag tillsammans med en kompis (elektriker, 20+ års erfarenhet, tidigare eget företag). Ursprungligen skrivet 2026-08-11 till 2026-08-20.

Rollfördelning: Jag hanterar mikroelektronik, firmware och programmering. Kompisen hanterar starkström, installation och praktiskt arbete.

docs.title: Affärsidé & Nischer
docs.text:
Planerade tjänster:

  • Batterireparationer — cellbyte i elcyklar, elsparkcyklar, laptops, elverktyg (Bosch/Makita)
  • Firmware-optimering — flasha om elcyklar (inom lagliga ramar), slippa dyra trimboxar
  • Reparation & service — elsparkcyklar, elcyklar, billjud
  • IoT & smarta hem — installation + konfigurering (han drar kablar, jag konfigurerar nätverk/appar)
  • Allmän elektronikreparation — datorer, telefoner, Li-Ion-celler, lödsvetsning

Målgrupp: föräldrar med barns trasiga elsparkcyklar, äldre/teknikovana som vill ha smarta hem-lösningar, folk som vill laga istället för köpa nytt.

docs.title: Företagsform & Juridik
docs.text:
!!! warning "Viktigast att lösa innan uppstart" Båda har skulder hos Kronofogden → enskild firma/handelsbolag är riskabelt eftersom intäkter kan utmätas direkt.

Alternativ som diskuterats:

  • Aktiebolag (AB) — bolaget är egen juridisk person, men styrelseledamöter måste vara "skötsamma" för vissa tillstånd.
  • Trovärdig kamrat utan skulder som formell ägare/VD, medan vi arbetar mot lön/konsultarvode. Kräver skrivet avtal och absolut tillit.
  • Börja som hobby/BDB eller under någon annans befintliga F-skatt som underleverantörer.

Nästa steg: Boka gratis första samtal med redovisningskonsult — förklara situationen öppet och se vad som är möjligt.

Säkerhet & regler:

  • Elsäkerhetslagen: Kompisen har behörighet, men se till att anmälan/egenkontroll sköts rätt.
  • Li-Ion-batterier: Brandsäker laddningsväska/gjutjärnsgryta, brandsläckare klass D + ABF, arbeta aldrig med skadade celler.
  • GDPR: Spara aldrig kunddata i Messenger/WhatsApp. Använd krypterad lagring. Skriv enkelt personuppgiftsbiträdesavtal om vi använder molntjänst.
  • Miljöfarligt avfall: Batterier och elektronikskrot till auktoriserad mottagare.
  • Dokumentera allt: Före/efter-bilder, kvitton, Swish/banköverföring (undvik kontanter).

docs.title: AliExpress 2026 — Så Funkar Det Nu
docs.text:
• Moms 25% gäller på allt utanför EU (sedan 2021).
  • Från 1 juli 2026: fast tull på 3 euro (~33 kr) per varutyp på paket under 1 655 kr.
  • Per varutyp, inte per paket: BMS + ESP32 + CH340 i samma paket = 3 varutyper = 9 euro i tull.
  • Från november 2026: EU-hanteringsavgift ~2 euro per försändelse.
  • IOSS: se till att säljaren har det (står i kassan), annars tar PostNord 100–250 kr extra.

Strategi: Samla till en stor order — färre varutyper = mindre tull. Större/dyrare prylar lönar sig mer (punktsvetsare, celltestare, lödstation). Småbeställningar under 200 kr har dött — blir dyrare än svenskt alternativ. Celler köps från NKON.nl (Nederländerna, ingen tull, snabb frakt, garanterat äkta).

docs.title: Batterier & 18650-celler — Arbetsflöde
docs.text:
Säkerhetsregler:

  1. Skadad cell (bukt, rost, varm) = kastas direkt.
  2. Ladda aldrig obevakat. Brandsäker väska eller gjutjärnsgryta med lock.
  3. Tejpa alltid pluspolen med isolertejp när cellerna ligger lösa.

Testa laptop-celler:

  1. Mät vilospänning: >3.0V = OK. 2.5–3.0V = testa långsamt. <2.5V = kassera.
  2. Ladda: 4.20V, 0.5A (500mA). Håll koll på värme.
  3. Vila 24h: mät igen. >4.10V = godkänd. <4.10V = hög självurladdning, kassera eller använd till ficklampa.
  4. Kapacitetstest: 12V bilglödlampa 21W eller 10 ohm resistor. Klocka tiden från 4.2V till 3.0V. Beräkna: Ah = ström(A) × timmar.

Ninebot G30-batteri efter 2 år:

  • Mät totalspänning: 36–42V = bra. Under 30V = öppna och mät varje cellgrupp.
  • BMS kan ha gått i djupvila — vissa väcks med "jump start" (avancerat).
  • Ninebot G30 är 10S4P eller 10S5P. Cellgrupper ska ligga inom 0.05V från varandra.

BMS: räkna seriekopplingar (S) — 10 celler i serie = 10S BMS. Ström: välj minst 30A kontinuerligt för marginal. Aktiv balansering helst, annars passiv.

docs.title: Ninebot G30 — Bygga Ihop Eller Sälja Delar?
docs.text:
Se även scooter för teknisk historik kring firmware/BLE på en annan Xiaomi-enhet.

Har: batteri (oklart skick, legat 2 år), motor, chassi Saknas: styrenhet (ESC): 800–1 500 kr, kablage: 200–400 kr, framdäck + slang: 150–300 kr. Totalt: ~1 150–2 200 kr.

Alternativ Intäkt Kommentar Sälja motor + batteri 1 100–2 700 kr Troligen ~1 500 kr, batteriet osäkert Bygga ihop hel sparkcykel 3 000–5 000 kr Investera ~1 500 kr → dubbelt så lönsamt

Beslutsträd:

  1. Mät batteriet: >36V och tar laddning = behåll och bygg ihop.
  2. Under 30V eller tar inte laddning = sälj motor + batteri som paket på Blocket för 1 000–1 500 kr, var ärlig med skicket.
  3. Om vi måste ha pengar till punktsvetsaren NU och har en kund som väntar = sälj, men försök låna/be förskott först.

docs.text:

docs.title: Termux På Samsung Tab A8 (Rootad)
docs.text:
Se phones-tablets för fullständig hårdvarustatus på surfplattan.

Användbara kommandon installerade:

pkg update && pkg upgrade -y
pkg install python git vim wget fzf zsh
pip install esptool pyserial
pkg install stlink openocd

Oh My Zsh – byt tema:

ls ~/.oh-my-zsh/themes/
omz theme set bira
sed -i 's/ZSH_THEME=".*"/ZSH_THEME="bira"/' ~/.zshrc
echo 'DEFAULT_USER="you"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

Anpassad prompt (lägg i ~/.zshrc):

PROMPT='%F{cyan}⚡%f %F{yellow}%~%f $(git_prompt_info) %F{green}$%f '

USB-OTG + programmering:

ls /dev/tty*                    # Se ansluten enhet
st-info --probe                 # Testa ST-Link
esptool.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 flash_id   # Testa ESP32
picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0  # Seriell monitor

Interaktiv pakethanterare (pkgu):

cat > $PREFIX/bin/pkgu << 'EOF'
#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash
if ! command -v fzf &> /dev/null; then
    echo "fzf saknas. Installerar..."
    pkg install fzf -y
fi
PKG=$(pkg list-all | fzf --prompt="Sök paket (ESC=avbryt): " --height=80% --reverse --header="Piltangenter=navigera | Enter=välj | ESC=avbryt")
[ -z "$PKG" ] && { echo "Inget valt."; exit 0; }
NAME=$(echo "$PKG" | awk '{print $1}')
echo "Valt: $NAME"
read -p "Installera? [Y/n]: " CONFIRM
CONFIRM=${CONFIRM:-Y}
[[ "$CONFIRM" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]] && pkg install "$NAME" -y || echo "Avbrutet."
EOF
chmod +x $PREFIX/bin/pkgu

Snabbkommandon för projektet (lägg i ~/.zshrc):

alias nb='cd ~/ninebot'
alias flash='esptool.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0'
alias st='st-info --probe'
alias ls='ls --color=auto'
alias ll='ls -lah --color=auto'
